content:
This was brought up ages ago, but I'm now wondering if we should revisit it. Currently, our specialization patterns allows you give lists of hypothesis names to a case, or a single (exact) hypothesis to a case. Not being able to construct a separating conjunction of terms inline feels missing, at least to my fingers, since I do this all the time with pure terms in Lean. Of course not as much of an idiom in Rocq, and there iFrame is good enough that this isn't a problem.

To ideas for extending specialization patterns to be more term-like: 1. allow nested specializations with the $$ syntax, and 2. allow exact constructions without first giving them a name.

Basically, I'm imagining we could turn 

  ihave H := iOwn_op (E := W.inv) $$ [H1 H2]
  · isplitl [H1] <;> iassumption
  ihave H := iOwn_cmraValid $$ H

into one line that avoids the extra naming and side-condition steps: 

ihave H := iOwn_cmraValid $$ (Own_op (E := W.inv) $$ (H1 ∗ H2))

What are your guys's thoughts? Please also feel free to tell me if I'm wildly underestimating the difficulty of this idea haha

Partly this comes up because when refactoring IProp proofs I notice that ihave either produces like five goals (for code like the one I showed above) or eight goals when I remove the E := W.inv. Lean solves all of these extra goals just by unification anyways once the side-condition proof is done. Combining patterns like I suggested above might help us avoid these sort of odd-looking fleeting side conditions.

It would definitely be nice to have, but I don't know how complicated it is. Probably more doable than in the Rocq version, since the selection patterns are extensible, but I haven't looked at the Proof Mode machinery yet, so can't be confident about that.

I think this would indeed be a very nice feature to have. My impression is that we would need support for framing at the pattern level to make this work smoothly. Since we do not have an implementation of iframe yet, this may have to wait a bit, but I agree that this idea is definitely worth keeping track of.
Maybe we should open a separate Zulip topic and start a small TODO/wishlist there, collecting the features people would like the Proof Mode to support

Markus de Medeiros said:

  1. allow nested specializations with the $$ syntax

This sounds indeed like a nice and useful feature. Lean (unlike Rocq) should in principle able to support this, but it might need some thought how to best resolve the mutual recursion between adding facts into the proof mode context and specializing them. But this should not be a fundamental blocker.

Markus de Medeiros said:

  1. allow exact constructions without first giving them a name

Maybe this is useful in some cases, but it is unclear how much this is necessary once we actually support iframe. Maybe this is best discussed again after iframe is implemented? (Note that I am currently working on adding iframe since it seems quite sorely needed.)
